title: Busan in 6 Days — Haeundae, Gijang, Nampo, Yeongdo
subtitle: Three nights in Haeundae and two in Nampo, with Gijang, Yeongdo and seaside cafés
summary: Six days in Busan, flying in and out of Gimhae Airport: Haeundae, the Gijang coast and Bokcheonsa, then Nampo-dong and Yeongdo. The notes cover the Busan Pass, transit cards, bus rules and tax refunds. The Yeongdo Bridge lifts at 14:00 on Saturdays by the official schedule, so on any other day you only see the bridge. Jeonpo Café Street, Taejongdae and Gwangalli sit in the alternates.

The coordinates for each spot are estimates.
What changed and what was cut

On day 1 of the travelogue you only reached Busan at 20:05. This template has you arrive around midday and moves everything earlier. On day 8 the travelogue took an early 10:50 flight home, and the template follows that.

Day 7 of the travelogue (Seomyeon: Lotte Department Store Busan flagship, Jeonpo Café Street, Kkotsalzip) overlaps with the shopping at Lotte Gwangbok on day 6, so only Gwangbok and Yeongdo are kept and Seomyeon goes to the alternates.

On day 5 of the travelogue, the Yeongdo Bridge was meant to lift in the afternoon and had been moved to the evening in summer. The template records the official Saturday 14:00 time; on any other day treat it as just seeing the bridge.
The travelogue did not get into Bokcheonsa because it had closed by the time they arrived. The template moves it to the afternoon, but still check the opening hours first.
Route

This template squeezes the 8-day, 7-night travelogue into 6 days: day 1 airport to Haeundae, day 2 Gijang and Cheongsapo, day 3 Spa Land, Centum City and the yacht, day 4 Nampo with Songdo, Gamcheon and Busan Tower, day 5 Bupyeong and Yeongdo, day 6 back to the airport.
The travelogue's Seomyeon plans (Jeonpo Café Street, Lotte Department Store Busan flagship, Kkotsalzip) and Taejongdae were not scheduled. Jeonpo Café Street and Kkotsalzip are in the alternates.
Getting between the airport and the city (Gimhae International Airport, PUS)

Light rail plus subway: about 5 min on foot to Airport Station, light rail to Sasang Station, then Subway Line 2 (the green line) to Haeundae Station. With the change it is about 55 min and about ₩2,800 (several roundup pages, 2026 data; the light-rail leg takes about 20–30 min but sources differ).

Airport Limousine No. 1 (Haeundae and Gijang): it goes over the Gwangan Bridge and stops at Haeundae Beach Station, with a bus every 60 min. Adults pay ₩9,500, with no transfer discount, and you must pay by card, not cash. The first bus from the airport is 07:10 and the last is 21:40. The travel time is not listed officially, and several roundup pages say about 60–80 min.
Airport Limousine No. 2 (Seomyeon and Jeonpo): adults pay ₩7,500. It stops at Seomyeon Station (Lotte Department Store), with the first bus from the airport at 07:00 and the last at 22:00.

You can reserve the limousine on the Bustago app, or buy at the ticket machine by Gate 4 on the first floor of the airport. Seats are not assigned, and when the bus is full you cannot board (Busan city announcement, 2025-07).
For the return trip: leaving from Jagalchi Station takes about 85 min. To take the limousine you need to change at Seomyeon (Line 2) first.
Busan Pass and tickets
The travelogue used the VISIT BUSAN PASS for Skyline Luge, Spa Land, the Songdo cable car, Busan Tower, the Beach Train and more. Compare it against your own mix of sights to see if it is worth it.
The Sky Capsule is not covered by the pass. You buy it separately and reserve a time slot, and it is very popular.
The yacht tour must be booked with the operator in advance. The night departure costs an extra ₩5,000 per person (from the 2025 travelogue), and you should be at the meeting point 30 min early.
Bus rules and transit cards
Busan bus rules: suitcases larger than 20 inches and hand-held drink cups are not allowed on board. Get on at the front door and off at the back.
For a transit card use a physical T-money card or T-money in Apple Wallet. Top it up in Taiwan first, or bring cash for the machines (they take ₩1,000 units).
In Korea use Naver Map for public transport. Google Maps navigation is not accurate there.
Highlights
Haedong Yonggungsa: the stairs at the signboard entrance are steep, and a gentle downhill path on the right leads straight to the main hall.
The Sky Capsule and the Beach Train are two different tickets. The Beach Train ticket you get from the pass lets you board once at any stop that day.
Bokcheonsa is a quiet temple and may close in the evening, so for a night view go to Busan Tower instead. The mountain road is steep, and the bus only goes to the foot of the hill.
Yeongdo Bridge lifting: Saturdays at 14:00 (official announcement). It was moved to the evening in summer once, so check the latest announcement before you go.
Photographing the airport runway in public spaces in Busan is prohibited (it is a joint civil and military airport).
Tax refunds

Korean tax refunds go through several companies' machines. Check which refund company is on your receipt and go to the matching machine. If you did not get the refund on the spot, you must claim your cash refund at the airport before you leave the country.
Entry
You can enter without a visa. Within 3 days before departure, fill in the online arrival card (e-Arrival Card): https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr
Pacing
Days 1 and 6 are airport days, so they are heavy on travel.
The template is based on a July–August summer travelogue, so sunset, the bridge lifting and opening hours change with the season.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 6 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Gimhae International Airport, with three nights in Haeundae and two near Jagalchi Station in Nampo. Haeundae, Gijang and Cheongsapo run on the subway, buses and trains; Nampo and Yeongdo on the subway and buses.
Day 1: land at midday, take the light rail and the subway to Haeundae, lunch at the traditional market, a walk on Haeundae Beach, then {@d1-05} at dusk and grilled eel for dinner.
Day 2: the Skyline Luge in Gijang in the morning, then {@d2-02}, the Beach Train to Cheongsapo in the afternoon and the Sky Capsule back to Mipo, with salt-grilled pork for dinner.

Day 3: the Shinsegae Spa Land jjimjilbang in the morning, lunch in the Shinsegae Centum City food court, the department store in the afternoon, a Busan yacht tour at dusk, and late-night snacks on Haeundae Gunam-ro.
Day 4: move to Nampo, Hong Kong Banjeom 0410 for lunch, the Songdo Marine Cable Car and Yonggung Cloud Bridge, then {@d4-03}, lid-grilled pork for dinner and Busan Tower at Yongdusan Park at night.

Day 5: Bupyeong Kkangtong Market in the morning, lunch and shopping at Lotte Department Store Gwangbok, the Yeongdo Bridge lifting, then {@d5-04} and Bokcheonsa Temple, and dinner around BIFF Square in Nampo.
Day 6: an early subway and light rail ride from Jagalchi Station to the airport for check-in and departure.
Where to sleep: three nights in a row near Haeundae Station, then two in a row near Jagalchi Station from day 4, opposite BIFF Square.

Getting around: from the airport to Haeundae, take the Busan–Gimhae Light Rail and then subway Line 2, about 55 minutes with the transfer and around 2,800 won; the airport limousine bus is the other option. In town it is mostly the subway and buses, with a T-money card, and buses do not allow suitcases larger than 20 inches. The Sky Capsule needs its own ticket and a booked slot, the yacht tour needs a booking with the operator, and the Yeongdo Bridge lifting time needs checking against the latest notice. The trip back from Jagalchi Station to the airport takes about 85 minutes, so leave early on day 6. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants Haeundae's beach, Gijang and Cheongsapo, old Nampo and Yeongdo in one trip. Every day involves the subway, buses and walking, so bring the legs for it; summer is very hot, so put outdoor sights early or late.
